title: Defining 2-group symmetries on lattices and extracting their anomalies
authors: Yitao Feng, Yu-An Chen
abstract_en: Ordinary $0$-form symmetries $G$ can mix with $1$-form symmetries $\Pi_2$ to form a $2$-group $\mathcal{G}$. We give a concrete lattice definition for a class of finite $2$-group symmetries in terms of local relations among symmetry operators. These relations identify the Postnikov class $[\rho]\in H^3(BG,\Pi_2)$ that characterizes the mixing. We develop a method to extract anomalies of these symmetries in one spatial dimension by restricting symmetry operations to an interval and comparing their composition near its endpoints. We also construct explicit qubit symmetry actions in $d=1,2,3$ spatial dimensions for a $2$-group with $G=\Pi_2=\mathbb{Z}_2$. These actions share the same nontrivial Postnikov class but include both anomaly-free and anomalous realizations. Their cohomological anomalies are classified by $H^{d+2}(B\mathcal G,U(1))$, which is $\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=1,2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=3$, and our constructions realize every class in these dimensions. Our results connect higher-group symmetry and its anomalies to concrete lattice operations, providing a microscopic framework for studying anomalous symmetries.

title: Quantum Foundations Beyond Bell's Theorem: A Topical Review
authors: Flavio Del Santo, Nicolas Gisin
abstract_en: We review a series of recent no-go theorems that extend the methodological and conceptual framework introduced by Bell's theorem to more sophisticated operational scenarios involving independent sources, quantum networks, joint measurements, and multiple observers. Many of these results were originally developed within quantum information science and are scattered across the literature, where their technical and application-driven success has partly obscured their broader foundational significance. We organize them around a common Bell-inspired methodology that extends beyond quantum nonlocality, and emphasize how increasingly rich operational structures change which physical assumptions can be tested.

title: Are quantum measurements universal?
authors: Massimiliano Sassoli de Bianchi
abstract_en: With D. Aerts, we showed in 2014, within the extended Bloch representation of quantum mechanics, that the Born rule can be understood as resulting from a universal average over all the possible ways in which the measurement-interactions can be selected. The cellular construction used there was since questioned, in the context of Bertrand's paradox, by N. Shackel, who observed that the result depends on the discretization adopted, that the sequence of averages is constant, and that the sense in which the average is taken over "all" densities remains unclear. Taking these criticisms as a stimulus, we re-examine the notion. The key is to recognize that a universal measurement is a random way of selecting a measurement which does not privilege any portion of the structure describing the available interactions, a property we call indifference. We prove that every indifferent universal measurement, however constructed, produces exactly the Born probabilities: the universal average is unique, and the cellular construction of 2014 is one among infinitely many ways of obtaining it, exact at every finite resolution. Non-trivial indifferent universal measurements exist, but must involve deterministic measurements: Dirichlet processes are indifferent universal measurements reaching every way of selecting an interaction, whereas an indifferent universal measurement free of deterministic components necessarily selects the uniform density, so that the Born rule holds not only on average but with certainty. Deviations from the quantum statistics in sequences of measurements are governed by a single parameter, in principle accessible to experiment. The only geometric inputs are the Euclidean length of the membrane and the orthogonal landing of the point-particle on it; the latter is where the content of Gleason's theorem lies. Generalizations to N outcomes and to Bertrand's paradox are discussed.

title: Ontology without states: PBR as an argument for dynamics-first realism
authors: Nick Ormrod
abstract_en: The Pusey--Barrett--Rudolph (PBR) theorem is commonly taken to establish that a pure quantum state represents a physical property of the system to which it is assigned, rather than merely encoding knowledge. In this work, I distinguish between state-first and dynamics-first physical theories, and argue that this reading presupposes the former. These two types of theories support different approaches to causal explanation, and one of PBR's stated assumptions depends on the state-first approach. Using a recent interpretation of quantum theory as a concrete example, I show how a dynamics-first theory can explain the PBR correlations while maintaining a broadly epistemic reading of quantum states. I conclude that the PBR theorem supports a dilemma: either the quantum state is part of reality, or reality is not fundamentally built out of states.

title: Quantum advantage by designing beneficial dissipation from lossless dynamics
authors: Zeng-Zhao Li, Xiao Xue
abstract_en: Passive loss removes probability from a system and therefore seems unable to improve an unconditional target. This intuition is exact for classical population dynamics under sink-only removal: passive killing obeys a finite-strength monotonicity principle even after optimization over the remaining controls. Here we show that coherent quantum dynamics can violate this classical monotonicity because coherent contributions to the final target can interfere destructively. We derive a trajectory-level criterion that determines when such a detrimental contribution is physically accessible to passive loss and accumulates into a net unconditional benefit. The criterion is encoded in a response operator constructed entirely from the lossless dynamics: its spectrum determines whether weak passive loss can help, while its principal eigenvector identifies the optimal environmental mode. Applying this criterion to vibronically assisted transfer, we identify a beneficial mode formed by coherently combining two individually detrimental local loss directions. The predicted mode remains near-optimal at finite loss, producing an \(8.73\%\) enhancement over the independently optimized lossless benchmark, compared with \(9.52\%\) under full finite-loss optimization. Our results establish how coherent quantum dynamics can evade classical passive-loss monotonicity and provide a general task-dependent principle for designing beneficial passive environments from lossless dynamics.

title: Competition and cancellation in a tilted Rice--Mele chain: exact Wannier--Stark offset and spectral readout
authors: Xiang Gao, Xing Deng, Shoulong Chen, Ying Zhang, Chunhua Zhang, Wei Xiao, Xueting Fang
abstract_en: In a tilted Rice--Mele chain, the Wannier--Stark (WS) ladder becomes staggered, \(E_n=n\Fo+(-1)^{n+1}A\). The offset \(A\) reflects the competition between the staggered onsite energy \(\Delta\) and the dimerized hopping \(\dt\), and its cancellation restores spectral equidistance. We determine \(A\) through a systematic strong-field series in the WS basis and a nonperturbative two-band Floquet expression. An exact matrix element reduces the strong-field expansion to Bessel algebra; at the representative working point, truncation at seventh order locates the cancellation point with a theory-internal truncation error of \(0.010\)~Hz, against \(27.3\)~Hz at first order. The Floquet propagator gives the closed form \(A=(\Fo/\pi)\arcsin(-i\,\mathrm{Tr}\,U/2)\), exact within the two-band model, implying the kinematic bound \(|A|\le\Fo/2\) and identifying cancellation with maximum spectral uniformity. The same analytic structure yields a family of real zeros and complex exceptional points that set the convergence radius of the strong-field series without touching the real axis. On odd-length chains, the hidden-symmetry defect produces a pairing plateau of height \(2|A|\) that persists numerically beyond first order in the modulations, allowing the offset to be read from the static spectrum without Floquet propagation or time evolution. In the bulk, cancellation appears as the merging of two sidebands into a single line at \(\Fo\), a null measurement that requires no calibrated sideband amplitudes, although the tilt and line frequency still need calibration. These signatures provide complementary spectral tests of the staggered WS ladder and a calibration-aware route to precision force sensing.

title: The geometry of Floquet states
authors: Vladimir Y. Cherynak, John R. Klein
abstract_en: This paper studies the moduli space of "good" periodic Hamiltonians, i.e., periodic Hamiltonians with nondegenerate Floquet spectrum. The corresponding Floquet states determine a geometric model for the moduli space of such Hamiltonians. The model is expressed in terms of configuration spaces, flag manifolds, and principal bundles. A corollary of the main result is the complete determination of the rational cohomology ring of the space of good periodic Hamiltonians. The paper also considers the adiabatic driving of a 1-parameter family of good periodic Hamiltonians. We formulate two conjectures describing the resulting asymptotic quantum evolution. These are Floquet analogues of the adiabatic theorem in quantum mechanics.

title: Conditional Information Flow and Neural Representability of One-Dimensional Rotated Cluster States
authors: Ziqi Xu
abstract_en: I study how measurement outcomes can remain conditionally dependent over long distances while the underlying state carries only a small internal memory, using one-dimensional rotated cluster states, whose exact matrix product state (MPS) bond dimension is $D=2$ at every rotation angle. Using exact MPS contraction, I compute the conditional mutual information (CMI) of two readout protocols: the entanglement-swapping endpoint CMI decreases from one bit at $\theta=0$ to zero at $\theta=\pi/2$, whereas a stationary bulk readout of the locally equivalent conventional cluster state vanishes at both limits. As an exact control, the spin-1 AKLT chain obeys $I_m=(4/9)\,3^{-m}$, so its CMI length equals its two-point correlation length, for an identifiable but non-generic reason. I then compare learners on the same $N=64$, $\theta=0.35$ target. A positive autoregressive GRU learns the computational-basis Born distribution from a few thousand samples, but an exactly computable Bell-basis readout shows that this distribution does not fix the phases. A complex RBM reaches the $N=8$ ground state under an exact objective, while a short generic recurrent variational Monte Carlo pilot is still improving when its runs end. As a positive control, an MPS-induced recurrent model whose hidden state is the bond vector reaches the ground state to near machine precision at $\chi=2$, whereas a $\chi=1$ control fails. These results show that long CMI does not require a large bond dimension, and that building the small virtual memory into the architecture greatly eases optimization.

title: Detection and Inhibition of Decoherence Through Collisions: A dynamical approach
authors: Sagnik Chakraborty, Srijon Ghosh, Federico Amato, Gniewomir Sarbicki, Dariusz Chru\'sci\'nski, Rosario Lo Franco
abstract_en: Quantum systems are intrinsically fragile and highly vulnerable to environmental noise, making the preservation of quantum states one of the fundamental challenges in realizing practical quantum technologies. We propose two noise-agnostic quantum state protection protocols based on a collisional model. The first protocol preserves quantum states of qubits without requiring complete prior knowledge of the underlying noise dynamics, and the second even protects a logical qubit under similar circumstances. These protocols provide robust protection for arbitrary single-qubit and entangled states against general noise processes. Furthermore, their capability to safeguard quantum states with an arbitrary number of qubits enhances the reliability, robustness, and scalability of emerging quantum architectures. These results establish the proposed framework as a promising approach for practical quantum information processing.

title: Maximum-Entropy Ensemble of Quantum Subsystems with a Fixed Average State
authors: Charlie Shakeshaft, Christopher David White, Harry J. D. Miller
abstract_en: The reduced density matrices of Haar-random bipartite states form a fixed-trace version of the Wishart ensemble of random matrices, with an asymptotic eigenvalue density given by the Marchenko--Pastur (MP) law. We establish a similar universal form for the maximum-entropy distribution of mixed states subject to a fixed ensemble average, arguing that its eigenvalue density converges asymptotically to that of the correlated Wishart ensemble (CWE). The density is thus obtained by a free multiplicative convolution formula, which we apply to the transverse-field Ising model (TFIM) with a thermal average state to derive a high-temperature leading-order correction to the MP law. We then consider measurement by a random POVM on the purification of the mixed reference state. We show that the resulting mixed-state ensemble is asymptotically equivalent to the CWE, and provide confirming numerical evidence. We return to the TFIM example to compute the entanglement of the system with the ancilla after measurement, and give finite-temperature Page curves for the average entanglement entropies.

title: Bath-state (In)dependence of Non-Markovianity Measures in Quadratic Open Systems
authors: Mirko Consiglio, Ilia Khomchenko, Tony J. G. Apollaro
abstract_en: Open quantum system dynamics fail to fulfill the conditions of the Markov approximation when the environment and system timescales are close to each other. Such behavior of these systems can be characterized by several non-Markovianity measures, which are expected to vary with the environment parameters. In this work, we consider a fermionic quadratic open quantum system, establishing bath-state independence of the Breuer--Laine--Piilo and the Lorenzo--Plastina--Paternostro non-Markovianity measures. However, our analytical results reveal that the entanglement-based and divisibility-based Rivas--Huelga--Plenio measures, as well as the entropic Megier--Smirne--Vacchini measure, remain sensitive to the reservoir state, through both its temperature and its chemical potential. Modeling the reservoir as a free-fermionic chain, we derive an exact time-local master equation for a single fermionic site in contact with it. Our numerical results for this model confirm these findings and show that the BLP and LPP measures vanish identically only on the bound-state threshold, where the bath-sensitive measures nevertheless remain finite.

title: Rapid mixing for Gibbs samplers for quantum spin systems with all-to-all interactions
authors: Nicola Bertoni, Giacomo De Palma
abstract_en: Understanding when quantum many-body systems rapidly converge to thermal equilibrium is a central problem in quantum statistical mechanics. While spatial locality provides powerful tools for systems with an underlying geometry, fully connected models require estimates that accommodate interactions between every pair of spins. We study Gibbs-state preparation for two-local quantum Hamiltonians on arbitrary interaction graphs, including fully connected systems, via Lindblad dynamics that satisfies Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance. Our approach is based on a quantum analogue of the classical Dobrushin condition, which controls the influence of local perturbations on the rest of the system. Using the quantum Wasserstein distance of order $1$, we quantify how these perturbations propagate under the dynamics and derive contraction estimates in a high-temperature regime controlled by the maximum total interaction strength per site. These estimates require no assumptions on spatial geometry or graph growth and yield mixing times logarithmic in the system size and the inverse error tolerance, uniformly over all initial states.

title: Characterizing Reaction Types through Linear Free-Energy Relationships in Cavities
authors: Jillian G. Hoffstadt, Davis M. Welakuh, Norah M. Hoffmann
abstract_en: Polaritonic chemistry holds the promise of controlling chemical reactivity through confined light-matter interactions, yet how reactions respond inside optical cavities remains debated. Here, we take a more zoomed-out view, inspired by electrostatic catalysis. We extend nonempirical linear free-energy relationships to cavity-modified reactions and show that their behavior falls into four distinct reaction types set by simple response-crossing rules. Reactions can follow conventional Bell-Evans-Polanyi (BEP) or counterintuitive Opposite-BEP behavior regardless of cavity tuning, or switch between the two as the cavity frequency is varied. We establish this picture analytically and demonstrate it in the Shin Metiu model and in four molecular reactions treated with ab initio electronic-structure methods. Even at this deliberately coarse-grained level, cavity-modified reactivity already shows qualitatively different and strongly counterintuitive behavior, including reactions that switch character with cavity frequency. Yet this complexity can still be reduced to a simple competition between permanent-dipole and polarizability responses. This reaction-type classification therefore provides a new route to organize and anticipate cavity-modified reactivity.

title: On the gauge-invariant orbital angular momentum of vector optical vortices in the paraxial approximation and beyond
authors: E. V. Maliutina, E. A. Vashukevich, V. A. Leonov, D. D. Reshetnikov, T. Yu. Golubeva
abstract_en: In this paper we present a gauge-invariant formalism for describing the spin and orbital angular momenta of scalar and vector optical vortices. The correction term, arising from consistent incorporation of the transverse vector potential's nonlocality, restores gauge invariance and makes it possible to separate the total angular momentum into spin and orbital components. We propose a method for calculating the orbital and spin angular momenta of multimode vector vortex fields and show that the orbital angular momentum of such beams contains two qualitatively different components. The polarization-independent contribution to the orbital angular momentum is related to the topological charge that determines the order of the phase singularity, while the polarization-dependent one is proportional to the helical topological charge that determines the spatial inhomogeneity of the polarization. We also discuss the quantization procedure for fields with spatially inhomogeneous polarization in terms of modes with a helical topological charge, and examine the limits of applicability of the proposed formalism.

title: Entanglement diagnostics of stochastic-resetting steady states: theory and measurement on superconducting qubits
authors: Jakob Murauer, Sabine Tornow, Manas Kulkarni, Eli Barkai, Satya N. Majumdar, Monalisa Singh Roy
abstract_en: Stochastic resetting drives quantum systems into nonequilibrium stationary states unreachable under uninterrupted unitary evolution, and their entanglement depends on whether the reset history is resolved or averaged over. We study this interplay in the transverse-field Ising chain, deriving closed-form results for two qubits and evaluating chains of up to 12 qubits exactly. In the two-qubit system, these closed-form results show that phase matching between energy eigenstates produces resonances, and their visibility in the stationary state is determined by the symmetry of the reset state. Measurements on an IBM superconducting processor show the entropies evaluated before and after the reset average closely following noiseless predictions with no fitted parameter, while concurrence lies below prediction across most of the hardware measurements. The two diagnostics respond differently because they read different components of the same reconstructed state, and a depolarizing model captures the concurrence suppression with one fitted parameter. The difference between the two entropies, i. e., the Jensen gap of entanglement entropy, equals the Holevo information that a subsystem retains about the time since the last reset. With a Bell-state reset, this information grows with chain length across a half-chain cut over the sizes studied, without visible saturation at the smaller reset probabilities. Since reset times are sampled and recorded classically, the trajectory-averaged entropy, and with it the Jensen gap, is obtained without postselection, in contrast to monitored circuits, where trajectory-resolved entanglement requires sampling exponentially rare measurement records.

title: Complex Langevin kernels for real-time SU(N) lattice gauge theory in 3+1 dimensions
authors: Kirill Boguslavski, Paul Hotzy, David I. M\"uller
abstract_en: We investigate complex Langevin (CL) dynamics for real-time SU($N$) gauge theories in 3+1 dimensions and introduce new kernel modifications tailored for lattice gauge theory (LGT). Using the anisotropic kernel as a baseline, we demonstrate that on a rectangular regularized Schwinger-Keldysh time contour, stable simulations are possible for pure SU(2) gauge theory up to a real-time extent of $2\beta$ at a bare coupling $g=0.5$, where $\beta$ denotes the inverse temperature. We show that a contour-dependent phase kernel extends this reach to $3\beta$, while a local, field-dependent kernel based on traced plaquettes achieves $3.5\beta$. These constructions represent the first application of such kernels to LGTs, especially in 3+1 dimensions. To validate the approach, we generalize the CL correctness criterion based on the drift magnitude to kernelled dynamics, providing a practical tool to assess correct convergence. Our results substantially advance the applicability of CL to real-time simulations in Minkowski space, establishing a framework for controlled studies of non-Abelian gauge theories at unprecedented time scales. A forthcoming paper applies these developments to the computation of unequal-time correlation functions.

title: Perspective on AI and quantum open-source software
authors: Changhao Li, Bradley A. Chase, Veena Vijayakumar, Mathys Rennela, Alessandro Cosentino, Naixu Guo, Sebastian Hassinger, Farrokh Labib, Seun Omonije, Patrick Rebentrost, Vincent Russo, Nathan Shammah, William J. Zeng, Ben Castanon
abstract_en: Quantum open-source software provides essential infrastructure for quantum science, and artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping its capabilities and transforming its development. However, verifying quantum software at scale remains difficult, and AI-generated contributions can increase the workload of maintainers. In this Perspective, we examine verification as a central requirement for reliable AI-assisted quantum software development and research. We analyze public repositories, records covering 110 repositories from five annual quantum open-source hackathons that we organize, and responses from more than 1600 participants in a community survey. Our analysis connects limitations in automated verification with the review burden on quantum software maintainers. We propose verification practices and contribution standards that require contributors to support their changes with reproducible evidence for maintainer review. We also examine how quantum open-source software can provide infrastructure for AI-driven research whose results the community can independently verify and build upon. We maintain an open-source companion repository to support reproducibility and help projects adopt and refine these proposals. Together, these contributions help the quantum open-source software community translate advances in AI into reliable quantum research through reproducible verification.

title: Probing micron-range fifth forces with cold atoms in optical tweezer arrays
authors: Marios Galanis, Andrew A. Geraci
abstract_en: We propose a new method to search for fifth forces at micron scales, by resonantly exciting the motional state of ground-state-cooled atoms in optical tweezer arrays. We develop a homodyne readout protocol based on sideband thermometry, which can approach the Standard Quantum Limit, and expand the discovery reach for fifth forces by up to four orders of magnitude compared to existing constraints. We show that this level of sensitivity can also probe well-motivated models of extra dimensions beyond the current tabletop state of the art, by leveraging the parametric enhancement of higher-dimensional gravity.

title: Quantum Observables of Nonperturbative Superradiant Scattering
authors: Asimina Arvanitaki, Savas Dimopoulos, Marios Galanis, Derek J. Li
abstract_en: Inelastic scattering from $N$ coherent spins, or any two-state system, scales as $N^2$, invalidating the Born approximation at large $N$ even at weak coupling. We develop a nonperturbative theory of this superradiant scattering and its backreaction on the spins. Since one particle can exchange many quanta, the target's energy-transfer and energy-variance rates keep their favorable $N^2$ scaling even after the cross section saturates, unless a conservation law limits each encounter to exchange of one quantum. We apply the theory to millicharged-particle searches, as well as neutron and charged-particle beams that can test quantum protocols for detecting cosmic relics.

title: A Primer on Instanton Physics - A Short Course
authors: Pervez Hoodbhoy
abstract_en: These six lectures, delivered at the University of New Brunswick 6-21 October 2026, are an introduction to instantons in quantum mechanics and quantum field theory for senior undergraduate and beginning graduate students. The first four lectures deal solely with particle mechanics, building the necessary background for the last two that cover applications in semi-classical field theory.

title: Mixed-State Topological Transition and Emergent Fractionalized Supersymmetry in the Non-Abelian Kitaev Spin Liquid
authors: Zhou-Quan Wan, Hong Yao, Shao-Kai Jian
abstract_en: We study a mixed-state topological transition in the non-Abelian Kitaev spin liquid driven by a bond-dephasing channel. In the vectorized picture, bond dephasing maps onto interactions between two time-reversed fractionalized Majorana systems coupled to gapped $\mathbb Z_2$ gauge fields, enabling sign-problem-free Monte Carlo simulations. We show that increasing dephasing condenses an inter-copy fermion pair, converting ${\rm Ising}\boxtimes\overline{\rm{Ising}}$ to toric-code order in the Choi state and yielding intrinsically mixed-state topological order upon unfolding. More interestingly, at a temporal interface between topological and trivial Kitaev states, a Chern-number mismatch enforces a gapless Majorana mode. Dephasing then drives a mixed-state topological transition at which the gapless mode develops emergent $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetry. Our Monte Carlo simulations yield $\nu=1.27(3)$ and $\eta_b\simeq\eta_f\simeq0.40$, consistent with the exact supersymmetric values $5/4$ and $2/5$. The supersymmetric partners are fractionalized and appear physically as distinct gauge-invariant spin strings, providing concrete observables for future experiments.

title: An Eigenvector-Continued Green's Function Method
authors: Stefano Brolli, Carlo Barbieri
abstract_en: Emulating the Green's function using reduced-order equations is challenging because of the amount of information it contains. This information includes the one-particle spectroscopy over the entire energy spectrum, the one-body density matrix, and the ground-state energy. Nevertheless, the computational speedup offered by emulators is essential for applications requiring repeated model evaluations, which are ubiquitous in many-body physics. These include parameter calibration, uncertainty quantification, phase-diagram mapping, and geometry optimization. In this Letter, we introduce a systematically improvable emulator based on eigenvector continuation and moment-matching. The resulting approximation, which we refer to as an ``eigenvector-continued Green's function,'' can be obtained by solving linear equations, enabling an efficient separation of the computational workload into offline and online stages.

title: A rhombic spin-1 interpretation of a room-temperature GaN emitter
authors: Daniel Hashemi
abstract_en: Single defects in GaN show optically detected magnetic resonance at room temperature. In the more abundant class, a minimal $S=3/2$ model leaves a $g\approx 4$ line unexplained. For one defect, this line lies near the sum of the two outer lines, consistent with transitions among three shared levels. A rhombic $S=1$ model reproduces the three line positions with rms errors of 8.1-9.8 MHz. The tested second-order $S=3/2$ fits containing all three transitions and the published minimal model do not reproduce these positions. A ladder fitted to the strong lines remains viable if the $g\approx 4$ line is a separate transition near the sum of the outer two. An unresolved frequency-window shift prevents the existing data from establishing the $S=1$ assignment uniquely. We propose a zero-field sweep that directly tests the isolated $S=1$ assignment.

title: Beyond energy bounds: comparing Schr\"odinger eigenstates
authors: Xiao-Ke Wang, Han Jia, Shengjun Wu, Zeng-Bing Chen
abstract_en: We derive eigenstate comparisons from ordered Schr\"odinger operators, extending energy bounds to overlaps, spatial distributions and nodes. For three form-ordered operators with discrete comparison ground states, suppose the upper ground-state energy lies in the lower operator's ground-state gap. Three comparison spectral values then bound all three squared ground-state overlaps and guarantee a simple discrete intermediate ground state. Related gap estimates control low-energy subspaces and individual excited-state overlaps under additional gap conditions. In one dimension and radially, a single crossing of the potential difference relative to the energy shift orders ground-state likelihood ratios and monotone observables; a nondecreasing difference suffices. The results cover asymmetric wells and shortened right Dirichlet walls, with coordinatewise comparisons for submodular reference potentials and coordinatewise nondecreasing perturbations. A two-sided Sturm argument orders corresponding internal nodes for nondecreasing potential differences, even between orthogonal one-dimensional excited states. For Yukawa ground states, Hulth\'en comparisons bound overlaps, radial moments and the density at the nucleus; the latter two-sided bounds hold for screening $0<\delta<2/\sqrt6$. Optimizing scaled Hulth\'en majorants gives a lower bound of approximately $1.13611$ for $n^2\delta_c(n,0)$, where $\delta_c(n,0)$ is the critical screening for the $n$th $s$-wave bound state. This bound is optimal within that two-parameter comparison family.

title: Quantum field theory with scale-dependent weighted measures: nonlinear momentum representations, vacuum fluctuations, and causal structure
authors: S. Gonz\'alez-Salud, R. Cartas-Fuentevilla
abstract_en: We reconsider the construction of free quantum fields through momentum-space weighted measures, introducing an independent energy scale that restores the conventional theory at low momenta. The resulting family is characterized by a dimensionless spectral function and includes, as a distinguished case, the spatial weight associated with the Euclidean Snyder algebra. We discuss its relation to modified dispersion relations and nonlinear momentum coordinates, and introduce an observer-covariant spectral weight defined using a timelike four-velocity. For the complex Klein-Gordon field we obtain the equal-time algebra, conserved weighted observables, vacuum fluctuations, and two-point functions in arbitrary spatial dimension. The ultraviolet conditions for their finiteness are established, and the nonlocal causal structure is analyzed in terms of a spatial convolution of the ordinary Pauli-Jordan distribution. An illustrative interacting extension and numerical profiles of the kernels and amplitudes are also presented.

title: P\"oschl-Teller type of Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonians: SUSY transformations
authors: \.{I}smail Burak Ate\c{s}, \c{S}eng\"ul Kuru, Javier Negro, Efe Serbest
abstract_en: The aim of this work is to define and investigate the generalized Jaynes-Cummings (JC) Hamiltonian by means of supersymmetric (SUSY) quantum mechanics methods. We have considered trigonometric and hyperbolic P\"oschl-Teller (PT) potentials as two natural ingredients to modify the standard JC model. We show that these generalized JC Hamiltonians have a list of characteristics in common with the JC Hamiltonian, for example: matrix intertwining, excitation number symmetry, Rabi frequency, formulas for atomic inversion and classical and revival times. Therefore, we conclude that JC Hamiltonians can be considered as one example of a wider a class of generalized Hamiltonians which can be useful in broader interaction problems.

title: QSoftCore: A Conceptual Foundation for Quantum Software Engineering
authors: Tao Yue, Yuechen Li, Man Zhang
abstract_en: Quantum software engineering (QSE) requires understanding application requirements, quantum programs and algorithms, quantum computation paradigms, executions, and deployment. However, relevant quantum computing (QC) concepts are often defined across physical, mathematical, and paradigm-specific levels of abstraction, making it difficult for the QSE community and hence proposed methods to refer to them consistently. To this end, we present QSoftCore, a conceptual model that reorganizes established QC concepts from a software engineering perspective and connects quantum applications, computational problems, algorithms, configurations, programs, and paradigm-specific computation specifications with state evolution, execution results, and backends. Our assessment against QSE literature across key software engineering activities indicates that QSoftCore provides shared QC referents for quantum computations, executions, deployment configurations, backends, and measurement evidence across the QSE lifecycle.

title: Non-Asymptotic Bounds via the Nussbaum-Szko{\l}a Mapping for Quantum Hypothesis Testing
authors: Jorge Lizarribar-Carrillo, Gonzalo Vazquez-Vilar, Tobias Koch
abstract_en: Quantum hypothesis testing concerns the discrimination between quantum states. This paper introduces novel lower and upper bounds for asymmetric quantum hypothesis testing based on the Nussbaum-Szko{\l}a mapping. Together, these bounds provide a unified recovery of both converse and achievability results across all major asymptotic regimes, including large-, moderate-, and small-deviations. Unlike existing bounds, which either rely on technically involved information-spectrum arguments or suffer from fixed prefactors and limited applicability in the non-asymptotic regime, the proposed bounds arise from a unified framework and enable, in some cases, the direct use of classical results. It is further demonstrated that these bounds provide accurate approximations to the optimal quantum error trade-off function at small blocklengths. Numerical comparisons with existing bounds, including those based on fidelity and information spectrum methods, highlight their improved tightness.

title: Nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics of a small quantum system coupled to quantum reservoirs
authors: Jeremy Schofield, Raymond Kapral
abstract_en: A statistical mechanical formulation where nonequilibrium averages of selected quantum observables are given exactly as averages over local density operators is used to describe the dynamics and thermodynamics of a small quantum system coupled to reservoirs. The local density operators are functionals of constraint variables that play the role of thermodynamic forces that satisfy a set of equations of motion. A focus of the work is on the evolution of the average internal energy of the quantum subsystem that may be subject to external autonomous driving that does work on the system, and on entropy production in the system. The nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics the quantum subsystem coupled to reservoirs, as well as that for the isolated subsystem and reservoirs, are discussed. When the subsystem is coupled to large quantum reservoirs, the effects of the quantum subsystem on the reservoirs can be captured through boundary conditions on the reservoir equations, and these boundary conditions are derived. The formulation is illustrated by considering the heat transfer through a system comprising a quantum system coupled to two heat reservoirs with different temperatures.

title: Distributed Inner-Product Estimation for Continuous-Variable Quantum States
authors: Jun Tang, Congcong Zheng, Xutao Yu, Zaichen Zhang
abstract_en: Distributed inner product estimation (DIPE) is a fundamental task in quantum information, aiming to estimate the inner product between two unknown quantum states prepared on distributed quantum platforms. For multimode continuous-variable (CV) systems, the infinite-dimensional Hilbert space poses an additional challenge. In this work, we develop a CV-DIPE protocol using only local homodyne measurements at shared phase settings and classical communication. Under a known bound on the mean energy per mode, we derive explicit finite-sample guarantees and sufficient copy counts for estimating the full inner product to prescribed accuracy and confidence. The energy constraint yields an inverse-square truncation-bias bound, while Gaussian structure strengthens the tail control to exponential decay and improves the resulting accuracy scaling. Numerical simulations with Gaussian and non-Gaussian states illustrate the balance between truncation bias and statistical error and its dependence on mode number and energy. Our results enable independent CV platforms to benchmark their state preparations against one another, even when neither state admits a tractable classical description.

title: Inevitability of the Petz transpose map
authors: Jacopo Surace, Chenxu Li, Francesco Buscemi
abstract_en: Bayes' rule is central to classical statistical inference: given a prior and a stochastic model, it determines the corresponding retrodictive conditional probabilities. In quantum theory, however, the question of whether an equally general rule of retrodiction exists and, if so, whether it is uniquely determined remains nontrivial. Here we prove that a retrodiction assignment defined for all priors and channels, which takes each predicted output state back to its prior, must coincide with the Petz transpose map if it is involutive, respects sequential and parallel composition, and agrees with unitary inversion. The theorem holds for channels between finite-dimensional full matrix algebras, with the input and output spaces restricted to the supports of the corresponding reference states. In particular, affinity under probabilistic mixtures and the characteristic square-root dependence on the reference states follow from these requirements rather than being postulated. Without involutivity, the remaining requirements characterize a family of doubly rotated Petz maps. Our result thus explains why the Petz transpose map arises in seemingly different areas of quantum theory: it is the unique quantum analogue of Bayes' rule compatible with these consistency requirements.

title: A density calculus for quantum field theory
authors: Tanay Kibe, Pratik Roy
abstract_en: These notes provide an introduction to Haagerup noncommutative $L^p$ spaces for quantum field theorists. The aim is to explain how the familiar calculus of density matrices, fractional powers, and Schatten norms extends to local observable algebras of type~III, where an intrinsic trace is unavailable. We develop the construction first for a matrix algebra, making the crossed product, its trace, and the dual action explicit, before passing to general von Neumann algebras. Particular attention is paid to the representation of normal states by Haagerup densities and to the distinction between the crossed-product trace and the canonical Haagerup functional used to compute expectation values. As a concrete application, we calculate the sandwiched R\'enyi divergence for a coherent excitation of a chiral current, verifying monotonicity under restriction and the R\'enyi quantum null energy condition at every real order $\alpha>1$. The presentation assumes familiarity with quantum mechanics and elementary quantum field theory, while introducing the operator-algebraic concepts needed for the construction and calculation.

title: Detuning-assisted cavity enhancement in spectroscopy
authors: Subhasish Guha, Sourav Das, Francesco Albarelli, Aiman Khan, Elnaz Darsheshdar, Adam D. Wright, Animesh Datta
abstract_en: Cavity-enhanced spectroscopy is a widely used experimental technique. We show that detuning the cavity frequency from the transition of interest can enhance the precision for dipole moment estimation by up to two orders of magnitude beyond the improvement when the cavity is resonant with the transition. We show this for both classical continuous-wave (CW) and pulsed single-photon probes, even in the presence of losses. We trace this enhancement to a detuning-controlled redistribution of information between the light- and matter-like polaritons, with losses determining the optimal branch. We show that this enhancement remains accessible using conventional photodetection and time-correlated single-photon counting.

title: QDMin: Coherent Quantum Minimum Finding for Nuclear Deformation Landscapes
authors: Abhishek, P. Arumugam
abstract_en: Locating the minimum of a nuclear collective landscape can require many interacting many-body calculations. QDMin (Quantum Deformation Minimum Finding) searches a parameterized Hamiltonian family with a coherent collective-coordinate register and an on-demand ground-energy threshold oracle. The oracle supplies the predicate required for quantum minimum-finding without first constructing the energy landscape point by point. We implement it for a schematic pairing-plus-multipole model using circuit-generated energy estimates during the search. In a four-point calculation, one Grover round raises the probability of the true minimum from 0.25 to 0.921. A $4\times4$ quadrupole--octupole-field calculation extends the complete circuit to two coordinates, although its minimum is first sampled in a round with zero Grover iterations. Its worst-case branch-preparation fidelity of 0.744 falls below the declared target, identifying coherent ground-state access as the current bottleneck. QDMin inherits expected $O(\sqrt{N_q})$ candidate-query scaling in the unstructured model; total advantage depends on the many-body oracle cost and remains unestablished.

title: A universal gauge structure in the photon content of light-matter systems
authors: Arka Dutta, Marcus Kollar
abstract_en: After truncating the matter Hilbert space of a single-mode light-matter model, gauge transformations leave the spectrum invariant whereas the ground-state photon number is gauge dependent, hence, its meaning remains disputed. We show that this gauge dependence obeys an exact algebraic law whenever the gauge transformation acts as a displacement of the field coupled to a matter operator $G$. Namely, the ground-state photon number is a quadratic polynomial in the gauge parameter $\lambda$, $\langle a^{\dagger} a\rangle_{\lambda}$ $=$ $\langle a^{\dagger} a\rangle_{0}$ $+$ $C\lambda$ $+$ $Q\lambda^2$. Here the coefficients are the correlator $C=\langle G\,p\rangle$ of $G$ and the field momentum $p$, and $Q=\langle G^2\rangle$. Its minimum over all gauges is naturally gauge-invariant, and for the quantum Rabi model it is determined by the ground-state energy alone. We show that it is strictly positive for the quantum Rabi and Dicke models with level splitting, so that a residual photon content survives in every gauge. At weak coupling the gauge of minimal photon number is the Jaynes-Cummings gauge, and for the Dicke model it remains so at all couplings in the thermodynamic limit.

title: Process matrices on generalised theories
authors: Matt Wilson, James Hefford, Timoth\'ee Hoffreumon
abstract_en: We extend the process-matrix framework for defining indefinite causal orders to a broad class of generalised physical theories. We give a simple re-axiomatisation of spacetime contexts in terms of naturality over classical probes, which precisely captures non-contextual assignment together with compatibility with convexity and coarse-graining within local laboratories. Using this compositional perspective, we give a clean characterisation of theories in which abstract spacetime contexts admit a process-matrix representation, and we pin down the precise conditions (satisfied by classical theory, quantum theory, and a Boxworld-like theory) under which the supermap and process-matrix perspectives on higher-order processes coincide.

title: Trajectory sharpening under quantum reference frame transformations
authors: Matteo Fadel, Giulia Gubitosi
abstract_en: Quantum reference frame (QRF) transformations relate the description of a physical system to different quantum observers, but their connection to concrete experimental phenomena remains largely unclear. Here we show that the trajectory-sharpening effect obtained by correlating a probed system with an effective negative-mass reference admits a natural interpretation as a QRF transformation to the frame of a negative-mass system. Using a minimal toy model of free particles with signed masses, we identify the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen-type observables responsible for this effect with a pair of commuting relational observables that, under the instantaneous QRF transformation, are mapped to operators local to distinct subsystems. We then show that the corresponding relational trajectory is reproduced by the dynamical QRF transformation, where the transformed relational position acquires an explicit time dependence. We introduce QRF-invariant sharpness measures for relational trajectories and derive monogamy relations showing that a trajectory cannot be made simultaneously arbitrarily sharp with respect to two distinct negative-mass frames. We further show that trajectory sharpness can instead reside in a collective reference mode encoded across two physical systems, even when neither constituent alone provides an arbitrarily sharp reference, so that sharpness can be distributed rather than localized in a single constituent frame. These results provide an operational, experimentally relevant interpretation of QRF transformations for continuous-variable systems.

title: Quasi-Phases of Quantum Matter
authors: Nick G. Jones, Paul Fendley, Nathanan Tantivasadakarn, Ruben Verresen
abstract_en: Within quantum many-body phase diagrams, continuous transition lines can appear and then terminate. However, it has remained unclear whether the neighboring regimes can be meaningfully described as distinct phases, akin to water and vapour, since any sharp characterization would have to go beyond the usual notion of phases of matter. We answer this in the affirmative by introducing quasi-phases: gapped regimes near a critical point that are connected in the broader phase diagram, but not by any gapped path accessible from small perturbations of the critical theory. The physical consequences include interface modes between regimes in the same phase of matter. More striking still, describing both the extended critical line and the gapped path connecting the regimes requires a bigger multicritical parent theory. In spin-chain examples with continuous terminating lines with central charge $c=1$, we find multicritical $c=3/2$ and $c=9/5$ orbifolds describing so-called 'quotient symmetry protected' and 'representation symmetry protected' topological phenomena. While one-dimensional symmetry-protected topological phases are labeled by projective representation classes, these quasi-phases can have interface modes carrying higher-dimensional linear representations. We turn this into a constructive principle through a weakening of the Lieb-Schultz-Mattis anomaly. Supporting distinct quasi-phases makes an unnecessary critical point infrared-necessary, even if it is unnecessary at the ultraviolet scale. This condition is more restrictive than simply having a codimension-one critical line, revealing richer structure within phases of matter than their conventional classification suggests.

title: Reconstructing hidden observables via quantum snapshot thermometry
authors: Jie Ren, Andrew Hallam, Luheng Zhao, Huanqian Loh, Zlatko Papi\'c
abstract_en: Projective snapshots are a standard readout tool for quantum simulators, but they directly probe only observables that are diagonal in the measurement basis. We show how local equilibration and an independently calibrated equilibrium equation of state can reveal otherwise hidden conserved-density profiles. We demonstrate numerically that such ``quantum snapshot thermometry'' can recover energy fronts and a diffusion constant, distinguish spin transport from energy spreading, and reveal conserved-charge profiles invisible in the initial measurements. We also identify symmetry-imposed ambiguities in the readout and show how prior knowledge of the spatial structure can resolve them. Fixed-basis snapshot thermometry thus provides quantitative hydrodynamic information beyond transport exponents, bypassing additional measurement bases and quantum state tomography.
